pages.text: The $(thing)Tobacco Drying Rack$() turns raw leaf into cured leaf. A rack holds up to $(item)16$() identical raw leaves. The tall wooden frame now occupies two block levels for placement and automation, but both halves are one shared rack inventory. Looking at either half shows the live $(item)X/16 Leaves$() count.

pages.title: Tobacco Drying Rack
pages.text: Craft the rack before choosing a curing environment.

Right-click the rack with raw tobacco to add one leaf. Empty-hand right-click removes the batch. Sneak-right-click reports detailed status. The visible rack progresses through empty, low, medium, and full load models. Once curing reaches $(item)10%$(), the batch locks and no more leaves may be added until it is removed or finished.
pages.title: Loading the Rack

pages.text: The rack automatically chooses the strongest valid method each tick in this order: $(thing)Fire → Flue → Sun → Air$(). You do not select a mode in a menu; the structure and environment select it for you. With Create installed, one fan airflow path reaching either rack level can assist a valid wooden-rack cure.
pages.title: Automatic Method
Industrial Drying Rack
pages.text: With $(thing)Create$() installed, the $(item)Industrial Drying Rack$() is a true two-block, 32-leaf automation-only factory rack. Both levels expose one inventory and top-down loading is allowed. Curing requires matching airflow across $(thing)both$() rack levels from two distinct Encased Fans; one fan or one-sided airflow is not enough.

pages.title: Traditional Alternative
pages.text: A Drying Rack is not required. Sneak-right-click the underside of a sturdy block while holding 16 matching raw or cured leaves to make a traditional hanging bunch. In Creative mode, one held leaf is enough to place the 16-leaf bunch. Raw bunches cure by the same methods; cured bunches can be hung for decoration/storage but expose no inventory automation or Display Link.

Vanilla hoppers can automate the wooden rack from either physical level. Insert raw leaves from a horizontal side; top and bottom cannot insert. A hopper underneath the lower half can extract only after curing is complete. The upper proxy also makes placing a block above the tall rack behave like a normal two-level structure.
